name: 406 Processing & Taxidermy

about:
Based in Great Falls, Montana, 406 Processing & Taxidermy operates as a locally owned whole-animal butchery. The business is owned and operated by award-winning taxidermist Dylan Lencioni, an avid hunter and fisherman who founded the company to serve the farmers, ranchers, and hunters of central Montana.

The facility provides year-round processing services for both wild game and livestock. During hunting season, the shop handles deer, elk, and antelope, while its livestock program offers on-ranch slaughtering—teams travel to the ranch to harvest animals and transport them back for cutting, wrapping, and specialty meat production. The taxidermy side produces European skull mounts using a beetle-cleaning method that preserves delicate bone structure, as well as full taxidermy mounts crafted by award-winning taxidermist Brad Lencioni.

Customers include Montana ranchers who need USDA-inspected or custom slaughter for cattle and other livestock, and hunters seeking reliable processing for their harvest. The company emphasizes that every carcass is tracked so clients receive meat from their own animal, a guarantee highlighted on its about page.

Differentiators cited by the company include the guarantee of meat identity, the convenience of on-ranch slaughter, the beetle-based European mount process that avoids bone shrinkage, and the reputation of its taxidermists for trophy-quality work. Lencioni frames the business as a family-oriented operation built on trust and personal pride in each step from field to table.
